mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows and increases risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns. This relationship is consistent across historical data and is not dependent on additional threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 225 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL is above 225 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) and strong employment growth (PAYEMS m/m growth > 0.5%) signals a tight labor market that accelerates inflation, prompting monetary tightening and leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% (m/m) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2.0%), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive 60-day forward returns due to sustained corporate earnings growth and investor confidence in the economic expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where GDPC1 annualized growth rate exceeds 2.0% over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 (index 2017=100) indicates a weakening manufacturing sector and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO is below 95.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 550 (thousands of units) signals a strong housing market and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to increased consumer confidence and business investment.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where HOUST exceeds 550.0 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of residential sales (RSAFS) above 350,000 million dollars compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns. This relationship is consistent and does not require additional threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS exceeds 350,000 million dollars over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 6.0%) signals a weak labor market and economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 6.0% over the last 5 years.
